steps.label: What a plasmid is
steps.margin_note: All four adjectives plus 'separate from the genophore'.
lines: A PLASMID is a small, SELF-DUPLICATING,
DNA fragment found in bacteria, separate from the
steps.why: Self-duplicating is the load-bearing word: because a plasmid copies itself independently, anything inserted into it is copied too.
common_mistakes: Saying a plasmid is the main bacterial chromosome. That is the GENOPHORE.
Leaving out 'self-duplicating'. It is what makes a plasmid useful as a vector.
steps.memory_tip: A small extra circle that copies itself.

steps.label: Its significance
steps.margin_note: Name the vector role and one more use. Four lines.

A gene inserted into a plasmid is carried into a

Plasmids also carry antibiotic resistance genes.
steps.why: A vector has to get into a cell and then multiply there, and a self-copying circle does both without any help.
common_mistakes: Giving only the definition. The significance is a whole mark.
Saying plasmids are essential to the bacterium. They are EXTRA; the cell survives without them.
steps.memory_tip: Put a gene in the circle and the circle copies it for you.
